name: EQT AB
reason: Alternative asset manager whose earnings hinge on fundraising, exits and carried interest (EBIT margin swung 60.3% in 2021 to 25.6% in 2022, EPS -37%), adjusted vs GAAP gap ~218% and LTM FCF yield only 1.1% vs 6.6% NTM; capital-markets earner like BX/ARES/HLNE.

name: DHL AG
reason: Express/forwarding earnings track global trade and freight rates: adjusted EPS EUR 4.33 (2022 peak) fell to 3.04 (2025, 0.7x peak) with 4.8% EBIT margin and only 3.4% 10y revenue CAGR; cyclical, low-margin and tariff-exposed with a residual German state (KfW) stake.

name: Smith & Nephew plc
reason: Share-losing orthopaedics/wound-care maker with adjusted EPS USD 0.85 (2015) to 1.02 (2025), a 1.8% 10y CAGR, ROIC averaging 7.8% and EBIT margin down from ~21% to 17.2%; a perennial turnaround with no record of compounding.

name: Quilter Plc
reason: UK wealth platform/adviser whose fees are set by market levels and flows (adjusted EPS GBP 0.12 in 2018 vs 0.11 in 2025, -25% in 2020), with ~4% ROE and policyholder-flow-distorted cash flow (LTM FCF yield 244%); capital-markets earner per the wealth-manager rule.

name: Amadeus IT Group SA
reason: GDS/airline-IT oligopolist with 27.8% EBIT margin, but earnings ride travel volumes (EPS EUR 2.95 in 2019 to -0.68 in 2020) and 2025 EPS of 3.20 is only ~8% above 2019; NDC direct-connect and AI-agent disintermediation are credible 5-yr threats to the distribution franchise.

name: Veolia Environnement SA
reason: Water/waste/energy utility-like group with ROIC averaging 2.7%, net debt/EBITDA 3.85x and EBIT margin at its 10y high (7.8%, 100th pctile) after the Suez merger lifted EPS from EUR 1.45 to 2.25; growth bought with leverage and shares (+2.6%/yr), regulated-style returns.

name: Wereldhave N.V.
reason: Benelux/French shopping-centre REIT whose FFO per share fell from EUR 3.45 (2016) to 1.85 (2025) with net debt/EBITDA 7.3x and consensus growth of 3-5%; levered retail property with no route to 7%.

name: Navigator Holdings Ltd.
reason: Handysize gas-carrier owner whose EPS (USD 1.76 in 2015, negative 2018-21, 1.18 in 2025) is set by charter rates and petrochemical trade; ROIC averaging 1.7%, cyclical shipping with no specialness.

name: Clarkson PLC
reason: Dominant shipbroker with net cash and research franchise, but earnings track shipping and newbuild activity: adjusted EPS GBP 1.06 (2020) to 2.85 (2024 peak) then 2.25 (2025, -21%), consensus FY2 -7% and LTG ~5%; cycle-driven and not forecastable.

name: ZEAL Network SE
reason: German online lottery broker with 26.8% EBIT margin, but EPS is erratic (EUR 2.97 in 2018, 0.08 in 2019, 2.70 in 2024, 1.98 in 2025), shares grew 9.7%/yr via the Lotto24 merger and the business depends on the German State Treaty on Gambling and state lottery licensing.

name: Halma plc
reason: Decentralised safety/environmental/healthcare instrumentation compounder with adjusted EPS GBP 0.34 to 1.14 (12.8% 10y CAGR, 9/10 years >=7%, worst year +2.2% in 2020), steady 17-21% EBIT margin, 13% ROIC and 1.2x net debt; bolt-on M&A (acq/FCF 0.74) is FCF-funded, and the NTM 6.4% FCF yield vs 3.0% LTM must be verified in the deep dive.

name: Billerud AB
reason: Paper-packaging and pulp producer with adjusted EPS swinging SEK 20.36 (2022) to 2.45 (2023) and 2.88 (2025, 0.14x 10y max), 2.6% EBIT margin and acquisition-led US expansion (acq/FCF 1.58); commodity-priced and ordinary.

name: UCB S.A.
reason: Biopharma whose adjusted EPS doubled to EUR 9.99 in 2025 on the Bimzelx launch after falling 33% in 2022 on Cimzia/Vimpat exclusivity losses; earnings depend on a few molecules, launch execution and pipeline readouts, with a 55% adjusted vs GAAP gap.

name: Compagnie de l'Odet SE
reason: Bollore-family holding at the top of a cascading listed structure (Bollore/Vivendi/UMG stakes, oil logistics, batteries) with GAAP EPS EUR 768.92 (2021), -352.26 (2022), -166.38 (2024) and EBIT margin -8%; opaque, deal-driven earnings and complex group governance.

name: Fagron SA
reason: Global leader in pharmacy compounding supplies with adjusted EPS EUR 0.68 (2017) to 1.25 (2025, ~7.9% CAGR) and stable ~15% EBIT margin, but ROIC averages only 7.9%, shares rose 8%/yr after the 2015-16 rescue rights issue, and demand depends on FDA/EU compounding rules and reimbursement.

name: Orkla ASA
reason: Nordic branded-consumer portfolio company (now restyled as an investment company) with adjusted EPS NOK 6.83 (2025) but 5y CAGR 6.3%, EBIT margin at the 27th pctile and consensus FY1-FY3 of -3.1%, +2.9%, +6.1%; mature local brands with no route to 7%.

name: FUCHS SE
reason: High-quality independent lubricant maker (ROIC ~17%, net cash) but adjusted EPS grew only 3.2%/yr (EUR 1.70 to 2.34 over 10y), EBIT margin drifted from 16.0% to 12.1% and consensus FY2-FY3 is 4.5-6.4%; base-oil cost exposure and EV transition cap growth below 7%.

name: Aon Plc
reason: One of three global broking/advisory oligopolists with adjusted EPS USD 6.18 to 17.07, rising every year (10.7% 10y CAGR), shares -2.6%/yr and 15% ROIC; the 2024 NFP deal (net debt/EBITDA 2.3x) is now seasoned, with margin at the 82nd pctile and softer P&C pricing as deep-dive tests.

name: Hexpol AB
reason: Polymer compounder serving auto/construction with adjusted EPS SEK 4.05 (2015) to 5.77 (2025, 3.6% CAGR), down from 7.51 in 2023 and EBIT margin at the 18th pctile; cyclical, raw-material-exposed and acquisition-dependent (acq/FCF 0.53) with growth below 7%.

name: ElvalHalcor Hellenic Copper & Aluminium Industry SA
reason: Viohalco-controlled copper/aluminium rolling and extrusion business with 4.5% EBIT margin, GAAP EPS EUR 0.42 (2022) to 0.08 (2023), FCF conversion 0.42 and shares +14%/yr from the merger; metal-price-driven earnings and group related-party structure.
